title: Hard Stop
intro: You can't cut what you can't stop, and stopping costs far more than going. This one is hard on your legs, and it brakes sideways, which is how you stop when you're pulled wide. You need a court or about twenty-five metres of flat ground with real grip, and court shoes. A slick surface is where an ankle goes. Mark each distance with tape or a line on the floor and pace it out first. Don't use cones or bags you could step on. No run-in is longer than ten metres. Do Landing Gear first if you haven't, because a brake is a landing you have to hold. It's twenty stops, seventeen of them at full speed, each with its own rest.

First time through, do half the reps in the last two blocks and take the full rest. Sore thighs and glutes for a few days is normal. Wait until the soreness has gone, and never less than 48 hours, before another hard running session or heavy leg lifting. Keep it two days clear of a match, before and after. Do it on fresh legs at the start of a training day. If a stop gets longer, wider or lazier than the one before, or your legs feel slow and heavy, end the session there. If you've ever torn a knee ligament, or you're coming back from an ankle injury, ask whoever treated you if hard stops and cuts are OK. If you have a sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles right now, or an injury has kept you off court in the last month, this isn't the session for today, so get it looked at first. Stop the session and get it checked if you get a sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop at the back of your thigh, in your groin, your calf or your Achilles. Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right means stop now and get it looked at before you train again. If a doctor has told you to be careful with hard exercise, check with them before you do this one. If you are far more sore than normal a day or two later, or your pee goes dark, get that checked the same day.

good: Jog easy until you're warm and breathing a little harder
Feel your legs loosen up with every minute
Drive the knee forward over your toes
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting the heel lift or the arch collapse

good: Step wide and sit back into that hip, chest tall
Feel the inside of the straight leg stretch
bad: Letting the bent knee cave inward

good: Step long, drop the back hip, then reach the inside arm up to the ceiling
Feel the front of the back hip and your upper back open up
bad: Rushing the reach before the hips have dropped

good: Shuffle ten metres each length, staying low and pushing the floor away with the trailing foot
Feel your thighs and glutes working to keep you low
bad: Bobbing up and down between steps

good: Add speed on each run, about 60, then 80, then 90 percent of your top speed
Fast but relaxed, never straining
bad: Going flat out on the first one

good: From tall on your toes, snap down into an athletic stance and freeze, as quietly as you can
Your hips go back and your knees soak it up
bad: Landing stiff-legged and taking it through your knees

good: Jog in, then kill the speed in two steps and hold the stance
Feel the last two steps getting wider and lower
bad: Slowing down gradually over five or six steps

good: Accelerate hard, then kill it in two steps and hold the stance
Feel your thighs and glutes absorbing the speed
bad: Braking on stiff, straight legs with your weight back on your heels

exercises.name: Lateral Run to Outside-Leg Stop
exercises.note: Do the first two at about three-quarter speed, then go flat out.

good: Run out about five metres to the side at full speed, then plant the foot on the side you're heading toward and stop
Feel the outside leg soaking it up, with your hips low and back
bad: Letting the plant knee cave inward

good: Run out about ten metres, brake over two steps, plant one foot and turn to sprint back
Your hips dropping as you brake
bad: Planting on a straight leg with your weight leaning out over the foot

good: Sprint in about ten metres at full speed, plant the foot opposite the way you're going and cut hard off it
Feel a firm push through the planted foot
bad: Planting your foot out in front of you on a straight leg
